title: CALIBUDGET: Calibration-Guided Source Allocation for Fixed-Budget Mixed-Reasoning Adaptation
abstract: arXiv:2609.36721v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Fixed-budget adaptation from heterogeneous data sources requires deciding not only how much data to use, but how much exposure each source receives. Size-proportional rules can crowd out small sources, whereas difficulty-only rules can chase noisy estimates or allocate residual budget to nearly saturated pools. We introduce CALIBUDGET, a floor-protected, reliability-aware integer allocator that treats source exposure as an explicit adaptation variable. From small train-internal calibration splits, it combines model need, post-floor availability, and bootstrap stability, then produces exact capacity-respecting quotas without changing the model, objective, or total budget. In a controlled setting combining mathematical and commonsense data, CALIBUDGET improves CommonAvg, FragileAvg, and MacroAvg over validation-error-with-floor, the strongest matched comparator, in all three paired LLaMA-2-7B LoRA+ runs. The respective mean gains are 0.56,

translated_title: CALIBUDGET：面向固定预算混合推理适配的校准引导式数据源分配
translated_abstract: arXiv:2609.36721v1 公告类型：new 摘要：在来自异构数据源的固定预算适配中，不仅需要决定使用多少数据，还需要决定每个数据源应获得多少曝光量。按规模成比例的规则可能会挤占小型数据源，而仅依据难度的规则可能会追逐带噪声的估计，或将剩余预算分配给几乎已饱和的数据池。我们提出了 CALIBUDGET，这是一种具有下限保护、可靠性感知的整数分配器，它将数据源曝光量视为一个显式的适配变量。该方法从小型训练内部校准划分中结合模型需求、下限保护后的可用性以及自助法（bootstrap）稳定性，然后在完全不改变模型、目标函数或总预算的前提下，生成精确的、符合容量约束的配额。在一个结合数学与常识数据的受控实验环境中，CALIBUDGET 在全部三次配对的 LLaMA-2-7B LoRA+ 运行中，均在 CommonAvg、FragileAvg 和 MacroAvg 指标上优于“验证误差加下限”这一最强的同类比较方法，平均增益分别为 0.56、（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出 CALIBUDGET，一种带下限保护、可靠性感知的整数分配器，通过从校准数据划分中评估各数据源的模型需求、可用性与自助法稳定性，在不改变模型、目标或总预算的情况下为异构数据源生成精确配额，从而在固定预算的混合推理适配中取得优于现有方法的性能。
en_tdlr: CALIBUDGET is a floor-protected, reliability-aware integer allocator that leverages small calibration splits to assess model need, post-floor availability, and bootstrap stability of each data source, producing exact capacity-respecting quotas under a fixed budget to outperform the strongest matched baselines in mixed-reasoning adaptation.
